sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bill in Bergen County, NJ?
sections.html:
Your town does. Bergen County is split into 70 municipalities (56 boroughs, nine townships, three cities and two villages), more than any other New Jersey county, and each one assesses its own parcels and collects its own tax. The county has one tax body, the Bergen County Board of Taxation, which sits at Two Bergen County Plaza, 1st Floor, Hackensack, and takes assessment appeals. Its number is 201-336-6300, and the county site also hosts a property record search and the board's 2026 to 2027 meeting schedule.

Hackensack, the county seat, is also the biggest municipality, with 46,030 residents in 2020. Mahwah is the largest by land, at 26.19 square miles. Oakland and Mahwah fall inside the Highlands preservation area, where extra state rules from a 2004 water protection law apply, so a seller there should ask the town what limits a buyer might face.

sections.h2: How does the Bergen County housing market look?
sections.html:
Bergen has the largest population of any New Jersey county. It had 955,732 people in 2020, the highest count in its history, and the 2025 estimate is 977,026. The latest five year survey results describe a costly, owner heavy market.

  • Half of owned homes are worth more than $623,000.
  • The middle household earns $124,884 a year.
  • Owners occupy 65.3 percent of households.
  • Housing units total 372,622, and 2,970 permits were issued in 2025.
  • Owners with a mortgage pay a median $3,547 a month, and those without pay $1,498.
  • Rent runs $1,914 a month.

Shopping is a local specialty. The Garden State Plaza opened in 1957 as New Jersey's first suburban mall, and Paramus's 07652 ZIP Code books more than $6 billion of retail sales a year. County blue laws keep most non food stores closed on Sundays, and Paramus adds stricter rules of its own. Hackensack University Medical Center is the largest employer, and the county's 2022 gross domestic product of $81.5 billion led the state.

sections.h2: What is Bergen County's geography and commute like?
sections.html:
The county occupies 246 square miles in the state's northeast corner, from the Hudson Palisades to the Ramapo Mountains. The Hackensack and Saddle rivers drain it, the Meadowlands wetlands fill the south, and three reservoirs, Woodcliff Lake, Lake Tappan and Oradell, supply drinking water to about 750,000 people.

Roads total nearly 2,989 miles, and towns maintain about 2,403 of them. The county holds the northern ends of the New Jersey Turnpike and Garden State Parkway, the eastern end of Interstate 80 and a stretch of Interstate 287. The George Washington Bridge ties Fort Lee to Upper Manhattan and is described as the world's busiest motor vehicle bridge. Census figures give a mean commute of 31.2 minutes.

sections.h2: What is the history and climate of Bergen County?
sections.html:
The area was home to the Lenape, including the Tappan, Hackensack and Rumachenanck groups, before Dutch settlers claimed it as part of New Netherland after Henry Hudson explored Newark Bay in 1609. The county dates to 1683. Its courthouse in Hackensack opened in 1912, and voters have elected a county executive since 1986. Today the county runs 21 parks covering more than 9,800 acres.

The climate is milder than in inland counties such as Sussex, partly because of the coastal location, lower ground and the shelter of the Watchung ridges. Hackensack averages a January low of 19 degrees and a July high of 86, with 3.2 to 4.6 inches of rain a month, and the county gets between 2,400 and 2,800 hours of sunshine a year.

sections.h2: When can you contest a Bergen County assessment?
sections.html:
Petitions go to the Bergen County Board of Taxation, which asks filers to use its online system. The cutoff is April 1, or 45 days after bulk assessment notices go out, and moves to May 1 when a town has revalued. The board's page says the 2026 window has closed, so the next opens with the 2027 notices.

Bergen County appeal checkpoints from the state's hearing guide
CheckpointDetail
Valuation dateOctober 1 before the tax year
Petition dueApril 1, or May 1 after a revaluation
Proof attachedSales of 3 to 5 comparable properties
Copies to assessor and board7 days before the hearing
DecisionWithin 3 months of the due date
Value freezeThe appeal year and the 2 after it

Source: New Jersey Division of Taxation, A Guide to Tax Appeal Hearings.

The county tells owners that today's assessment is presumed right. You must show it exceeds market value, and a bill cannot be appealed because the tax comes from the local budget.

sections.h2: What proof helps at a Bergen County hearing?
sections.html:
The state wants market value on the October 1 valuation date, supported by sales that closed before that day. Assessments of similar houses are not accepted as proof.

  • Three to five recent sales of homes like yours.
  • Photos of your house and each comparable.
  • An income statement, for commercial property.
  • An appraisal or repair estimate where the house has flaws.

Attend the hearing. The board rarely grants delays, and missing it can produce a judgment for lack of prosecution that closes the door on the Tax Court of New Jersey. Where a town has not revalued lately, the board also measures your assessment against a band of 15 percent either side of the district's average ratio.

sections.h2: Which schools and colleges serve Bergen County?
sections.html: The county has roughly 45 public high schools and at least 23 private ones. Bergen County Academies, the public magnet school in Hackensack, is frequently ranked among the best in the country. Colleges include Bergen Community College in Paramus, Fairleigh Dickinson University in Teaneck and Hackensack, Felician University in Lodi and Rutherford, and Ramapo College in Mahwah. Your town's clerk can tell you which school district a given street belongs to.

sections.h2: What should a Bergen County seller do about taxes before closing?
sections.html:
Request a payoff from your town's tax collector, not the county. The title company or closing attorney wants to know which quarterly installments are paid and what interest is owed. Quarters in Brick, to name one town, fall on February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, and your own collector will confirm local dates.

  • Ask your attorney how the contract splits the quarter in which you close.
  • Report any addition you built, since added assessments can create an extra bill.
  • If an appeal is still pending, decide in the contract who gets any refund.

Older residents and disabled owners may qualify for a $250 deduction through Form PTD, renewed each year with Form PD5 by March 1. The Division of Taxation's Property Administration unit takes questions at 609-292-7974 or 609-292-7975.

faqs.q: Who is paid the property tax in Bergen County?
faqs.a: The tax collector of your own municipality, not the county. All 70 towns run their own billing and payment methods, and the county board in Hackensack hears only assessment appeals.

faqs.q: By when must a Bergen County owner petition against an assessment?
faqs.a: By April 1 of the tax year, or within 45 days of the bulk mailing of notices. Where a town revalued, the date is May 1. The county board says the 2026 window has closed.

faqs.q: Where can a Bergen County owner reach the Board of Taxation?
faqs.a: The office is at Two Bergen County Plaza, 1st Floor, in Hackensack, and the number is 201-336-6300. In person filing is accepted, though the county prefers online petitions.

faqs.q: What if a Bergen County owner skips the tax hearing?
faqs.a: The board can enter a judgment for lack of prosecution, which can bar a later appeal to the Tax Court. The state guide says adjournments are normally denied.

faqs.q: Can a Bergen County house sell while a tax quarter is unpaid?
faqs.a: Yes. Back taxes and interest are paid from the seller's share at closing, using the payoff the municipal collector supplies. Get that figure before you fix a closing date.
